# 1 Enoch Chapter 94 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles

---

**1** And now I say to you, my sons: love righteousness and walk in it, for the paths of righteousness are worthy of acceptance, but the paths of unrighteousness shall suddenly be destroyed and vanish.

**2** And to certain men of a generation, the paths of violence and death shall be revealed, and they shall hold themselves far from them and not follow them.

**3** And now I say to you who are righteous: Do not walk in the paths of wickedness or the paths of death; do not draw near to them, lest you be destroyed.

**4** But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and a life that is elect, and walk in the paths of peace, and you shall live and prosper.

**5** Hold fast my words in the thoughts of your hearts, and do not allow them to be erased from your hearts; for I know that sinners will tempt men to do evil to wisdom, so that no place may be found for her, and no temptation of any kind may diminish.

**6** Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression and lay down deceit as a foundation, for they shall be suddenly overthrown and shall have no peace.

**7** Woe to those who build their houses with sin, for from all their foundations shall they be overthrown and shall fall by the sword. And those who acquire gold and silver shall suddenly perish in the judgment.

**8** Woe to you, the rich, for you have trusted in your riches, and from your riches you shall depart, because you have not remembered the Most High in the days of your riches.

**9** You have committed blasphemy and unrighteousness, and you have prepared yourselves for the day of slaughter, the day of darkness, and the day of the great judgment.

**10** Thus I declare and point out to you that He who created you will overthrow you, and there will be no compassion for your fall, and your Creator will rejoice at your destruction.

**11** And your righteous ones in those days shall be a reproach to sinners and the godless.

---

*LOGOS notes: Chapter 94 opens the sustained series of woe oracles (chs. 94–100). The woe formula ("Woe to those who...") echoes the prophetic tradition of Amos, Isaiah, and Micah. The targets are the wealthy who exploit others (vv. 6–10), a central concern of the Epistle. The statement "your Creator will rejoice at your destruction" (v. 10) is deliberately shocking — a reversal of the Psalmist's "not desiring the death of the wicked."*
